A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Self Forcing research work, with readable main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, user preferences, training-efficiency measurements, and controlled ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original quantitative comparisons, user-study results, qualitative video evaluations, and ablations, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: Self-rollout training, gradient truncation, DMD/SiD/GAN objectives, rolling KV caching, and local-attention training remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are identical; the deleted cache strategy was an unsuccessful alternative, not a component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same VidProM-based training coverage, synthetic training videos, VBench evaluation, MovieGenBench user study, and video-extrapolation scenarios.

E2.justification: Section 3.4 removes the narrative comparison with a tested StreamingLLM-inspired strategy that keeps the first frame fixed while rolling the remaining cache. The comparator sets in the tables and figures are unchanged.

E3.justification: Model configurations, four-step generation, prompt preprocessing, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and single-H100 timing remain unchanged. Appendix E still specifies 1003 MovieGenBench prompts with one user evaluating each prompt.

E4.justification: v2 removes the brief report of testing fixed-first-frame cache retention as an alternative extrapolation strategy. Table 2's controlled ablations, Figure 6's efficiency analysis, and Appendix B's local-attention ablation remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the user-study sampling description remains identical.

E6.justification: v2 deletes the qualitative finding that the StreamingLLM-inspired cache strategies proved ineffective for video generation. Numerical and plotted results are unchanged, including Table 1's chunk-wise score of 84.31, throughput of 17.0 FPS, and latency of 0.69 seconds.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, complexity arguments, and Appendix A equations are unchanged. Changing the GAN description from 'approximates' to 'approximately minimizes' Jensen–Shannon divergence clarifies the existing objective without revising the formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions and claims about reducing exposure bias, holistic distribution matching, efficient rolling KV caching, and real-time generation with competitive quality.

C2.justification: The exposure-bias explanation, first-latent distribution-mismatch rationale, and limitations concerning long-video degradation and gradient truncation are unchanged. The deleted cache sentence removes a reported observation rather than revising these interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 3 retain the same implementation sources, noise schedules, hyperparameters, prompt-processing instructions, hardware, and training times. The project link and user-study instructions are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the specific negative comparison with a StreamingLLM-inspired video adaptation. Reference [92] and its acknowledgment as inspiration remain, and the bibliography and dedicated Related Work section are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits comprise the GAN wording clarification, deletion of the failed-cache sentence, added funding acknowledgments, removal of the correspondence line, and publication-status updates. Section organization and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title-page footer changes from a preprint notice to NeurIPS 2025 information, the correspondence footnote disappears, and nearby text and spacing reflow. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The unchanged algorithms, quantitative evidence, principal ablations, limitations, and appendices preserve the paper's scientific support and reproducibility. v2 clarifies the GAN wording and adds funding disclosure while losing a brief, unquantified failed-cache observation. These limited changes do not materially alter overall paper quality.
